dineshba/tf-summarize.title: feat: add moved resource support to all writers
dineshba/tf-summarize.body:
- Closes #95
- Relates to #88

Previously, moved resources were only shown in the Table and HTML writers (via a separate GetAllResourceMoves() code path), and FilterNoOpResources() actively stripped them before other writers could see them.

This unifies moved resource handling across all output formats:

- Preserve moved resources in FilterNoOpResources() so they survive the no-op filter (alongside the existing import preservation logic)
- Add "moved" to the GetAllResourceChanges() map, which automatically propagates to SeparateTree and JSONSumWriter
- Add IsMove() method to the Tree type and a moved branch in GetColorPrefixAndSuffixText() (ColorCyan / "(→)" suffix), enabling Tree and JSON writers to render moved resources
- Handle moved resources in the JSON writer's treeValue(), outputting PreviousAddress as the diff value
- Remove the separate GetAllResourceMoves() function and its dedicated code paths in Table/HTML writers — moved resources now flow through the same GetAllResourceChanges() map as all other change types
- Add deterministic ordering to HTML templates by iterating over an explicit order slice instead of ranging over Go maps, addressing the same class of nondeterministic output ordering reported in #88
- Show resource count on moved rows in table output (e.g. "moved (2)") for consistency with other change types

dineshba/tf-summarize.title: chore: streamline CI/CD process & automatically release from main
dineshba/tf-summarize.body:
This addresses https://github.com/dineshba/tf-summarize/issues/101.

- make is the unified entrypoint for building, testing, linting, and releasing across both local dev and CI/CD
- make itself uses `goreleaser` for testing, building, linting, and releasing `tf-summarize`
- versioning is driven by a `VERSION` file's value; CI/CD verifies that PRs/commits bump the version value via an [ensure-unpublished-release](https://github.com/mdb/ensure-unpublished-release-action/) job; this can by bypassed if either 1) the commit author is dependabot or 2) the commit contains the text `[skip release]`
- BONUS: upgrades Go, upgrades GH Actions, address various gosec & lint complaints

See individual commits for further details. For an example of an analogous CI/CD pipeline, see [terraputs's CI/CD workflow](https://github.com/mdb/terraputs/actions/runs/21862929658).

dineshba/tf-summarize.title: feat(table, HTML): include 'moved' resources
dineshba/tf-summarize.body: This addresses issue #95 for the table and HTML writers, which now include summary of "moved" resources. This does not include moved resources for the other writers given those writers are a bit more minimal in their summary, which doesn't even include output changes.

dineshba/tf-summarize.title: support `-html` flag to render output as HTML
dineshba/tf-summarize.body:
This addresses issue #69 to support HTML output.

This also...

- updates the README usage docs
- validates that multiple, conflicting format flags are not provided
- fixes a bug in the tests to properly validated expected errors invoking `tf-summarize`
- improves the `tf-summarize` tests to exercise the tool's ability to summarize changes to outputs (as well as resources)
- improves `make help` to output documentation for all Makefile targets 
- improve test accuracy via `-count` flag, protecting against false positives in `go test` runs

Seed plant for the future: Ultimately, it might be preferable to support a single `-format="json|md|html|table"` flag, though I was hesitant to do so in this PR and break `tf-summarize`'s existing usage in a non-backwards-compatible fashion.

dineshba/tf-summarize.title: Fix issue #20 "unexpected end of JSON input" error
dineshba/tf-summarize.body:
This fixes issue #20 by correcting the `reader.CreateReader` logic determining whether to use a `reader.FileReader` or `reader.StdinReader`. Previously, in some environments (like GH Actions Ubuntu runners), `tf-summarize` incorrectly attempted to use a `reader.StdinReader`, even when an explicit filename argument is provided.

Ideally, `tf-summarize` would feature automated tests through which I could prove the bug & fix. ~In absence of such tests,~ I added a `demo` GitHub Actions job proving `tf-summarize` continues to work. ~However, I'm happy to add real tests (either in this PR, or in a followup PR)~, if you prefer those, @dineshba (I'm also happy to remove the `demo` GH Actions job from this PR if you prefer it not clutter `.github/workflows/build.yml`).

**Update:** I added 2 additional commits:

* https://github.com/dineshba/tf-summarize/pull/64/commits/40f8d1bd71529351c5b051a032fc5f3d646f0960 ensures the use of a consistent Terraform version when interacting with the `example` project
* https://github.com/dineshba/tf-summarize/pull/64/commits/efdf4dbd5ff3364c0f39ed0f6bbb70c7ecba92df adds an automated test verifying the fix provided by this PR showing that `tf-summarize -md plan.json` and `cat plan.json | tf-summarize -md` both continue to work as expected.

Note that https://github.com/dineshba/tf-summarize/pull/63 shows reproduction of the bug via a similar GitHub Actions-based demo.

dineshba/tf-summarize.title: Demo reproduction of issue 20
dineshba/tf-summarize.body:
In absence of tests, this is an attempt to demo [issue 20](https://github.com/dineshba/tf-summarize/issues/20)'s reproduction.

It is not my intent that this be merged :)

dineshba/tf-summarize.title: ensure multiple markdown tables are rendered
dineshba/tf-summarize.body:
This seeks to fix issue #61 by printing all output to the `io.Writer` passed to `writer.TableWriter#Write`. This ensures multiple, distinct markdown tables are printed, even when `tf-summarize` is invoked with both `-md` and `-out` flags.

Previously, `fmt.Println()` was used to separate the markdown tables, but this is insufficient when `-out` is used with a non-STDOUT writer, as is the case when writing output to a `-out`-specified file.

samsarahq/go.title: fix: don't strip 'src' from filepaths
samsarahq/go.body:
Beginning with its initial commit (https://github.com/samsarahq/go/commit/237936dc7ac826df5f3cbb2d54e0ec6705060051)
8 years ago, `oops` strips anything up to and including a `/src/` from
filepaths in stack frames. For example, files like `go/foo/bar/src/baz/bim.go`
appear as `baz/bim.go` in stack frames.

In addition to being somewhat confusing and arbitrary (depending on
codebase/expections), this also seemingly breaks [Datadog source code
integration](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/guide/source-code-integration/);
Datadog is unable to use [git metadata](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/guide/source-code-integration/?tab=githubsaasonprem#embed-git-information-in-your-build-artifacts)
embeddd in telemetry to properly link to GitHub files.

This seeks to change that.

Signed-off-by: Mike Ball <mikedball@gmail.com>

* standardize scripts/*.sh on 2 space indentation
* double quote various shell script vars to prevent globbing and wordsplitting and to satisfy [shellcheck](https://www.shellcheck.net/) complaints

Thanks! 
### Motivation
* Previously, these scripts had a mix of tabs/spaces, with inconsistent indentation. While not a functional problem, this made for kind of an icky developer experience.
* Previously, these scripts were vulnerable to globbing and wordsplitting (plus, the `shellcheck` complaints create noise for contributors whose editors are integrated with `shellcheck`)

DataDog/dd-trace-go.title: chore: remove unnecessary Error() calls
DataDog/dd-trace-go.body:
### What does this PR do?

This is a NOOP cosmetic change that seeks to improve the developer experience (for contributors, as well as for users who vendor dd-trace-go).

In fmt.Errorf calls, the %s verb already calls Error() on error types, making the explicit call unnecessary. Tools like Cursor Bug Bot (and probably some editor tools too) complain about the redundant Error() calls; this satisfies the complaints.

...it also means users who vendor `DataDog/dd-trace-go` and who use Cursor Bug Bot (or other code review automation tools) aren't subjected to these tools' complaints about the redundant Error() calls littering pull requests. So, this helps minimize that litter.

### Motivation

My organization vendors dd-trace-go in our own codebase(s); this improves the developer experience, particular around dd-trace-go upgrades.

keidarcy/e1s.title: speed up services rendering by recycling pages
keidarcy/e1s.body:
After a cluster's services page has been initially rendered, this speeds up subsequent visits to that page by re-using the original, already-rendered page (and avoids redundant AWS API requests).

While PR #126 helped reduce the initial service page rendering to 4-5 seconds in clusters hosting 400-500 services, this reduces subsequent service page rendering to < 1 second.

As a tradeoff, service page data is no longer guaranteed to be fresh with each page render, though <ctrl+r> continues to reload the data.

keidarcy/e1s.title: Configurable log file path
keidarcy/e1s.body:
This seeks to offer a quick/dirty/stop gap alternative to PR #124 that:

1. Ensures `e1s` works on Window by using an OS agnostic technique for
   setting the debug log file path (Currently, I don't believe `e1s` works on Windows)
2. Enables users to configure their own debug log file path via a
   `-log-file-path` CLI option in instances where the default `os.TempDir()`-homed
   log file path is undesired.

However, beyond this stop gap PR -- ultimately -- I'd love to see `e1s`...

* support a properly configurable logger that respects different
  log levels
* surface errors to users via the UI (rather than swallow them)
* allow its own logs and diagnostics to be browsed within its UI

However, this seeks to offer an intermediary solution.

keidarcy/e1s.title: perform describe services API requests concurrently
keidarcy/e1s.body:
Rendering the "services" page can take an extremely long time for clusters with many services. Analysis shows `api.Store#ListServices` is the culprit. On clusters hosting ~450 services, the `ListServices` method **took > 20 seconds** to complete. Now, using concurrency, `ListServices` **takes < 5 seconds** to complete against those same clusters.

This also bubbles up previously-ignored errors pertaining to the describe services API requests.

ljfranklin/terraform-resource.title: add `terraform-provider-vinyldns`
ljfranklin/terraform-resource.body:
@ljfranklin This is a bit of a long shot -- and I completely understand if you'd rather not do this -- but this PR seeks to build the [terraform-provider-vinyldns](https://github.com/vinyldns/terraform-provider-vinyldns) into `ljfranklin/terraform-resource` such that users don't need to download it separately.

The context is...

My organization runs a very large Concourse installation serving thousands of developers. Your `ljfranklin/terraform-resource` is very popular and is in use throughout users' pipelines. However, because many, many pipelines _also_ make use of the [terraform-provider-vinyldns](https://github.com/vinyldns/terraform-provider-vinyldns), it's necessary for users to download and install the `terraform-provider-vinyldns` plugin on execution of each job that utilizes it, which tasks the pipelines in doing a lot of perhaps-avoidable work. 

For example:

```yaml
- name: terraform-apply
  serial: true
  plan:
  - in_parallel:
    - get: source
    # a github-release-resource instance:
    - get: terraform-provider-vinyldns
    # a task that copies the terraform-provider-vinyldns and .tf files to a shared location
  - task: install-tf-plugins
    file: source/ci/tasks/install_tf_plugins.yml
  - put: terraform
    params:
      terraform_source: tf-src-and-plugins
```

Before forking your resource (thanks again for all your hard work on it!), I figure I'd _at least_ open this pull request to gauge your feelings (But, as I said, I completely understand if you'd rather not merge it).

Thanks!

The js errors you are experiencing are related to code outside the scope of this example. Specifically, it seems as though you have a mix of Node.js- and browser-based JavaScript in your app.js file. My example does not require any server-side or Node.js-based code.

Please let me know if you have any questions.

Hope this helps!

Thanks,
Mike
